text:
I, yes—but what of the evening star, rising and descending

from the heavens, weary and forgotten?

And the poor, who knocked at doors, to no avail, making

night and day tremble with their dry fists?

And the children, crying with terrified hearts: ‘why

does no one answer us?’

And the roads, and the empty roads, with their hands stretched

out uselessly?

And the motionless saint, who lets things go on their way?

And the musics shut in boxes, sighing with wings

folded?


Ah!—I, yes—because I have already wept everything, and dismissed my

used, sad body,

and my tears washed it, and night’s silence dried it.

But the dead, who buried dreamed of light

doves and bright flowers,

and those in mid-sea who thought of the message the shore

would swiftly unroll to their fingers…

But those who fell asleep from too much vigil—and whom I

do not know whether they will wake…

and those who died of waiting too long…—and whom I do not know were saved.


I, yes. But all this, all these eyes fixed on you, high

in life,

I do not know whether they will look at you as I do,

reborn and stripped of vengeance,

the day you need forgiveness.

translation.title: Letter
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of a Portuguese original. The broken interrogative syntax and final conditional are preserved.
